backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param groups before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Change the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from its current value to 3 and separately test 7 in a replicate. Keep the quintic coefficients as they are. This trades optimizer compute for orthogonalization accuracy, which changes effective per-step throughput within the fixed 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz iteration count 3 vs 5

backlog.spec: Set the Muon momentum update to plain heavy-ball momentum (no Nesterov lookahead) by turning off the nesterov flag in the Muon optimizer construction and in the update formula. Everything else, including the orthogonalization and the LR, stays the same. This checks whether the lookahead term helps at this short training horizon.
backlog.title: Disable Nesterov in Muon

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon learning rate per matrix by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so that tall matrices (for example MLP up-projections) get a proportionally larger step, rather than using one global MATRIX_LR for all shapes. Compute the factor once per parameter when building the param groups. Keep MATRIX_LR as the base value.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling

backlog.spec: Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 while leaving all other learning rates unchanged. The current embedding learning rate is very aggressive for Adam and may be causing noise early in training. This is a single-constant change that isolates the embedding optimizer's contribution.
backlog.title: Lower embedding LR

backlog.spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalar parameters (residual and skip mixing scalars) that use Adam. Leave the matrix, embedding and unembedding learning rates unchanged. Large scalar learning rates can make the residual gains oscillate, so this checks whether a gentler scalar step improves convergence.
backlog.title: Lower scalar LR

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.99) for the Adam-optimized parameters. Keep the Muon momentum unchanged. A higher beta2 gives a longer variance memory, which may stabilize the very high embedding and scalar learning rates.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99 for non-Muon parameters

backlog.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before the optimizer steps, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. Log nothing new. This guards against occasional loss spikes that waste steps in a 300 s run with high learning rates.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown over the last WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the time budget with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC times the peak, computed from elapsed time over the budget. Apply the same multiplier to every parameter group. Keep the warmup and budget logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so that the learning rate begins decaying earlier and spends more of the 300 s budget at reduced LR. Keep the linear shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. This tests whether a longer anneal improves the final checkpoint quality.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown fraction

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps linearly from zero over the first 2 percent of the time budget before the plateau and warmdown. This protects the high initial learning rates from destabilizing early Muon and Adam updates while keeping most of the budget at peak LR.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the learning rate anneals to 10 percent of its peak instead of zero at the end of the budget. The warmdown shape is otherwise unchanged. A small nonzero floor can help the last steps make progress rather than stalling.
backlog.title: Nonzero final LR fraction

backlog.spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 and set ASPECT_RATIO to 51 so the model dimension stays near 512 (10 times 51 is about 512, rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM). Keep HEAD_DIM, window pattern and all other settings the same. This tests whether extra layers at similar width beat the current shallower model within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Depth 10 with fixed model width

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so the model dimension grows to roughly 512 with fewer layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and the rest unchanged. Fewer layers run faster per step, so this tests whether more tokens seen in 300 s outweigh the loss of depth.
backlog.title: Shallower and wider model

backlog.spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so each attention layer has twice as many heads of half the width, with the model dimension unchanged. Adjust nothing else. Smaller heads often give better per-parameter attention quality at small scale and may help the short run.
backlog.title: Head dimension 64

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSLL" so half of the layers use full causal context rather than one quarter. Keep the final layer full-context as the existing code requires. This trades some attention compute for better long-range modeling in a small model.
backlog.title: Window pattern with more full-context layers

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy, computing logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) on the lm_head output in both training and evaluation paths of the forward pass that the training loop uses. Only the training forward pass is changed; do not touch the evaluation call. This bounds extreme logits and often stabilizes the high learning rates used here.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Add a learnable per-layer scalar that mixes the first layer's token embedding output into each attention value projection, so v = v + lambda_i * x0 where x0 is the normalized input embedding and lambda_i is initialized to zero. This gives each layer direct access to the token identity signal. Parameters use the existing scalar optimizer group.
backlog.title: Value-embedding residual mixing

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP nonlinearity with relu(x) squared, so the MLP computes down(relu(up(x))**2). Keep the hidden width and projection shapes unchanged. This activation is cheap and often improves loss per step in small transformers trained for minutes.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation

backlog.spec: Apply RMSNorm without learned gain to the query and key tensors per head immediately before the attention dot product, if the current code does not already do so. This keeps attention logit scale bounded as learning rates grow. Keep the rotary embedding applied as before, after or before the norm consistently.
backlog.title: Parameter-free RMSNorm on Q and K

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention block and each MLP block to zero, so every residual branch starts as identity at step zero while the rest of the initialization is unchanged. This makes early optimization smoother for the very high learning rates in use. Verify the Muon update still applies to these matrices.
backlog.title: Zero-init residual output projections

backlog.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic unchanged so that the number of accumulation steps halves. More optimizer steps fit into 300 s, which may help a model that is still improving quickly.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch size

backlog.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens per optimizer step by doubling gradient accumulation with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE fixed at 64. Fewer, less noisy steps may give a better gradient signal per update for Muon. Keep all learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger total batch size

backlog.spec: When TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE changes, scale EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR and SCALAR_LR by the square root of the batch ratio relative to 2**19, and keep MATRIX_LR unchanged since Muon is less sensitive to batch. Implement as a single computed factor applied when building the Adam param groups. Use this together with a batch size change.
backlog.title: Scale learning rates with batch size

backlog.spec: Train on shorter sequences early and longer ones later: for the first 30 percent of the time budget use half the context length by splitting each batch into two halves along the sequence dimension, then switch to full length. Keep the total tokens per step constant. This increases early step throughput, and the training data loader interface is not to be changed beyond the batch reshape.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Make the Muon weight decay scale with the current learning rate multiplier from the schedule, so that the effective decay per step is WEIGHT_DECAY times the current LR divided by the peak LR. Apply the same rule to the decoupled weight decay step. The rest of the Muon update is unchanged. This reduces decay pressure during warmdown when the weights should settle.
backlog.title: Weight decay tied to LR

backlog.spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 for the Muon matrix parameters. The current decay is strong for a run of only 300 s, so this checks whether the model is being underfit. Leave all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower Muon weight decay

backlog.spec: Add a z-loss term of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the logits to the training loss, which keeps the output logit normalizer near zero and reduces logit drift. Compute it from the same logits used by the cross-entropy during training only. Do not change evaluation.
backlog.title: Logit z-loss regularizer

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Use the averaged parameters for the final model state that the harness evaluates, by copying the EMA weights into the model just before the end-of-training evaluation call. Do not alter the evaluation call itself.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights

backlog.spec: Speed up each training step without changing the model math by enabling TF32 matmuls and cuDNN benchmark mode at startup, and by ensuring the model is compiled once with dynamic=False so that the first step does not recompile on the last partial batch. Verify that the seed lines remain exactly as they are. The goal is more steps in the 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Compute throughput tuning

backlog.spec: Set the output projection to share the token embedding matrix (lm_head.weight = wte.weight) and drop the separate lm_head parameter. Use EMBEDDING_LR for the shared tensor and ignore UNEMBEDDING_LR. Keep the 1/sqrt(model_dim) scaling on logits if the code has it. This frees about vocab x model_dim parameters, which can be reinvested in depth or width under the same 300 s budget. Lower-priority option: if untied-only scaling is in use, keep the init std equal to the embedding init.
backlog.title: Tie embedding and lm_head weights

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 256 so the 512-dim model has 2 attention heads of width 256 instead of 4 of 128. This is the opposite direction from the rejected HEAD_DIM 64 run (i015). Keep all other hyperparameters and the window pattern unchanged. Confirm that the flash-attention or SDPA path supports head dim 256 on A100 before the run; if it does not, fall back to 192 or drop the idea.
backlog.title: Head dimension 256

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 in the rotary frequency computation. Leave the rest of the attention code and the sliding-window pattern unchanged. With a 2048-scale context and short training, a larger base lowers the frequencies of the slow dimensions and can help longer-range position signal. Cache cos and sin in the same dtype as before so there is no extra memory cost.
backlog.title: RoPE base frequency 100000

backlog.spec: Add one learnable scalar per attention head, initialized to 1.0, that multiplies the query vectors after RoPE, or equivalently scales the attention logits. Put it in the scalar (Adam, SCALAR_LR) parameter group, with no weight decay. Keep the standard 1/sqrt(head_dim) scaling in addition to this factor, so the initial behavior is unchanged. This lets each head learn its own sharpness at negligible cost.
backlog.title: Learned per-head QK temperature

backlog.spec: Scale the learning rate of each transformer block's matrix parameters (both Muon and Adam groups) by a depth factor, lr_l = base_lr * (0.85 ** (DEPTH - 1 - l)), so the last block gets the full rate and the first block gets a smaller one. Embedding, lm_head and scalar groups are unchanged. Implement this by setting per-group lr values when building the optimizer param groups. Keep the warmdown schedule multiplying all groups the same way.
backlog.title: Layer-wise learning-rate decay across depth

backlog.spec: During training only, drop each block's attention and MLP residual branch independently with probability p = 0.1 scaled linearly with depth, so the first layer has p = 0 and the last has p = 0.1. When a branch is kept, scale it by 1/(1-p) to preserve expectation. Disable this in evaluation and in the final model used for val_bpb. Each step sees a randomly thinned network, a regularizer that may help on this short run with a small model.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on residual branches

backlog.spec: Add one auxiliary head that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state, using a separate linear projection that shares the embedding dimension. Train with total loss = CE(next token) + 0.3 * CE(token at t+2), where the auxiliary term is computed only over valid positions. Use the main lm_head for the primary term unchanged. Drop the auxiliary head at evaluation time so the reported val_bpb uses only the next-token head. This gives an extra training signal per forward pass.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary loss

backlog.spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 for the first 40% of the time budget and then switch to 2**19 for the rest. Implement this by computing the gradient-accumulation step count from elapsed time each optimizer step, so the micro-batch size stays at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and only the accumulation count changes. Keep the learning rate schedule unchanged. The ramp gives more optimizer steps early when learning is fastest.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp from half to full

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a step schedule: hold the full LR multiplier 1.0 until 60% of the time budget, then drop to 0.2 for the rest of training, applied to all parameter groups. Keep WARMUP_RATIO = 0. This tests whether a long high-LR plateau followed by a sharp drop beats the current continuously decaying schedule. Do not change any other hyperparameter.
backlog.title: Two-phase step decay LR instead of linear warmdown

backlog.spec: Keep a running uniform average of the model parameters, in fp32 on the GPU, taken once per optimizer step during the last 20% of the time budget. At the end of training, copy the averaged weights into the model before the harness evaluation call and leave the evaluation code untouched. This is a snapshot average over a fixed window, not an EMA over the whole run. Keep the averaging buffer out of the optimizer so it cannot affect training dynamics.
backlog.title: Average checkpoints over the final 20% of training

backlog.spec: In the Muon optimizer step, after the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization of each matrix update, divide each output row by its own RMS (or L2 norm), then rescale the whole update so its overall RMS matches the current uniform Muon scaling. Keep the momentum, Nesterov, weight decay and LR schedule unchanged, and apply the change only to the matrix parameters that already use Muon. This equalizes update magnitude across neurons, which the uniform Muon step does not do. Keep the code to a few lines inside the existing Muon update function.
backlog.title: NorMuon: per-row normalization of Muon updates

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam groups for embeddings, lm_head and per-layer scalars with a schedule-free variant. Keep a fast iterate z updated by Adam, and an averaged iterate x = (1 - c) * x + c * z with c = 1 / (step + 1) capped at a small constant, with gradients evaluated at the interpolation y = (1 - beta1) * z + beta1 * x. Drop the linear warmdown for these groups, since the averaging replaces it. Muon parameters keep their current schedule. Evaluate and save using x for these groups, so the final weights are the averaged ones.
backlog.title: Schedule-free AdamW for non-matrix parameters

backlog.spec: Keep the model width unchanged and build 3 unique transformer blocks, then apply the stack of 3 blocks twice (6 effective layers) with the same weights. Keep the window pattern defined per effective layer and give each pass a learned scalar that scales the residual so the two passes can differ. This cuts the parameter count by half at the same compute, so it tests whether a smaller unique-parameter budget with extra effective depth is better for a 300-second run. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: Shared-weight recurrent depth

backlog.spec: Change the attention so that queries keep their full number of heads but keys and values use only 2 heads, shared across query groups by repeating them before attention. Keep HEAD_DIM and the rotary embedding the same, and apply QK normalization as before. This reduces the K and V projection cost and memory, which may increase training throughput within the fixed 300-second budget and so allow more optimizer steps. Keep the rest of the model and the optimizer unchanged.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with 2 KV heads

backlog.spec: After scaled dot-product attention and before the output projection, multiply each head's output by a learned gate sigmoid(W_g x), where W_g is a small linear layer from the residual input to one scalar per head, initialized so that the gate starts near 1 (for example with a bias of +2). Apply no other changes. This adds a cheap input-dependent gating of attention heads that can suppress unhelpful heads and aid optimization in a short run. Keep the parameter group of the gate on the Adam path with the same LR as the other matrices, or on Muon if it is 2D, and state which.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid gate on attention output

backlog.spec: Change the MLP hidden expansion from 4x to 3x the model dimension in every block, and reinvest the saved parameters and compute by increasing the number of layers by one while keeping ASPECT_RATIO and HEAD_DIM rules so that model_dim is unchanged. The aim is to test whether extra depth at lower MLP width gives better loss per second in this short training regime. Keep all optimizer and schedule settings the same. If the resulting parameter count is far from the baseline, report it and keep the change to this single adjustment.
backlog.title: Narrower MLP with 3x expansion

backlog.spec: Apply rotary position embeddings to only the first half of each attention head's dimensions and leave the second half unrotated, so that some channels carry position-invariant content matching. Keep the RoPE base frequency and everything else the same. This is a small change to the attention position encoding that is easy to isolate, and it may help on short contexts where rotation of all channels is not needed. Make sure the split is applied consistently to both queries and keys.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embedding on half the head dimensions

backlog.spec: Replace the single linear warmdown with a schedule that runs two cosine-decay cycles across the 300-second budget. Each cycle decays the LR from its peak to 0.1 times the peak, and the second cycle restarts at the peak LR and decays to the final LR at the end of the budget. Keep the warmup at zero and keep the Muon momentum schedule unchanged. The restart may let the model escape a flat region and spend more time at a useful LR before the final decay. Base the schedule on elapsed training time, not step count, to match the existing budget logic.
backlog.title: Two cosine warm-restart cycles over the time budget

backlog.spec: During training only, randomly replace 5 percent of the input token ids with a fixed mask or unknown id before the embedding lookup, and compute the loss on the original, unreplaced targets. Keep the output targets unchanged so the model still predicts the true next token. Evaluation and the final summary are unchanged. This is a light regularizer that forces the model to use context more, and it adds no parameters or compute. Use a single constant such as TOKEN_DROP_P = 0.05 at the top of train.py so the change is easy to revert.
backlog.title: Input token dropout as regularization

backlog.spec: In the training loss, compute per-token cross-entropy for each micro-batch and average over all tokens, but multiply the loss of tokens whose loss is in the top 25 percent of the batch by 1.5 before averaging. Leave the weights for the other tokens at 1.0 and detach the weighting mask so gradients flow only through the loss. Evaluation is unchanged and the reported metric is computed by the harness on the model, not on the training loss. This focuses gradient signal on hard positions, which may help the bits-per-byte metric in a short run. Keep the optimizer and schedule the same.
backlog.title: Hard-example loss reweighting by top-k token loss

incumbent.description: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 to fit more optimizer steps within the 300s limit, potentially allowing longer training at a smaller batch.

memo: Helped: smaller batch size and architecture shape. TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 gave 1.0688 and 1.0579 over 2 runs (-0.0385 vs the previous incumbent), though it carries a tripwire flag, so check that before trusting it. The shape change (DEPTH 6, ASPECT_RATIO 85) scored 1.1019 (-0.0126). Did not help: optimizer and schedule tweaks (SCALAR_LR 0.25 +0.0024, Muon momentum ramp +0.0076, per-matrix Muon LR +0.0013, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 +0.0052, step decay +0.0108), batch 2^20 (+0.0008), DEPTH 10 (+0.0333), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0140), auxiliary multi-token head (+0.0192), query scale (+0.0022). EMA scored 2.2581, likely a bug. Slots 6 and 8 failed to patch, so copy SEARCH text exactly. Next: continue the batch axis (2**17), re-tune LR and warmdown at the smaller batch, try DEPTH 5 with wider dims, and replicate the half-context curriculum (1.0980). Keep changes small.
